idea-plugin.name: LogPose
idea-plugin.description:
LogPose — see what your Android app is actually doing, right in the IDE

LogPose turns your app's runtime behaviour into a clean, structured timeline inside a tool window — network, pushes, database, background work and feature flags — and lets you mock any response straight back to the device. No proxy, no certificates, no adb logcat | grep: a one-line OkHttp interceptor emits each exchange and the plugin reassembles it.

Your coding agent can read the running app

LogPose exposes the live capture over MCP, so Claude Code — or any MCP client — reads the running app and you just ask: "what failed in the last 2 minutes?", "which worker ran 20 times on startup?", or "mock /v1/orders to return a 500 so I can see the error UI." Real traffic, not a log line you pasted. Click ⚡ Connect Coding Agent to copy the command; it serves on the IDE's built-in web server, localhost only, authenticated with a per-project token that also selects which project's capture to read.

  • Read — list_events, get_event, get_trace, find_failures, session_summary
  • Follow one id — get_related returns every event carrying a business id (order_id 21053953) as a timeline, across traces and including rows with no trace at all; list_correlation_keys says which keys this project uses
  • Diagnose — query_hotspots, worker_history, config_changes: "what's making this screen slow?", "did SyncWorker retry?", "what flag changed before this broke?"
  • Change what the app receives — create_mock, set_mock_enabled, delete_mock, list_mocks, plus list_scenarios / load_scenario / save_scenario for whole bottled sessions, so an agent can reproduce a state and verify its own fix without you driving the UI
  • Start a flow and wait for the result — inject_fcm delivers a synthetic push into the running app and await_event blocks until what it triggered arrives: trigger → await → assert, with no polling
  • Response bodies can be withheld while still exposing request shape, statuses and timings

Capture

  • One row per HTTP exchange — request and response together, never interleaved, never cut off by logcat's ~4 KB line limit
  • Firebase Cloud Messaging pushes and token refreshes appear inline in the same timeline, so you can read push → API call → UI as one story
  • Database, background work and remote config — Room queries show their operation and table, a WorkManager request occupies one row that updates as it runs and badges its retries, and a remote-config activation reports exactly which flags changed with before → after values
  • Your own events — LogPose.event("UserDao.insert") { … } puts any subsystem on the same timeline; events carry their own presentation, so they render with no plugin update
  • Duplicate detection flags repeated calls and likely double-submits

Inspect

  • Collapsible JSON trees plus a real IDE JSON editor (folding, line numbers) in Raw mode
  • One-click filters: URL search and type toggles (NET / FCM / DB / WORK / CONF / ANLY / APP) always on the bar, with method, status, hide-noise and duplicates-only a click away in the Filters popover — every active choice echoes as a removable chip
  • Copy as cURL, copy JSON or a response body, find within a body
  • Multi-select rows and copy the call sequence as plain text — ideal for bug reports
  • First-class multipart upload (S3 / GCS) metadata instead of raw bytes

Mock & replay

  • Right-click any captured request → Mock this endpoint and serve a response without touching backend or app code
  • Replace the whole body, or merge your JSON into the real response: override one field, add keys, and let everything else stay backend-generated
  • Edit the response field by field — fold what you don't need, tick exactly what to override, and see the original value beside your change
  • Inject latency, timeouts and connection failures, cap how many times a rule serves, and match paths with * wildcards
  • Narrow a rule to requests carrying particular query parameters, headers or body text, and serve a different response per hit — a 500 then a 200 tests retry logic in one rule
  • Rules sync to the device over adb, report live hit counts, and clear themselves when you stop capturing — mocked rows are badged, so the timeline never lies about what the app actually received
  • Save a rule set, or a whole recorded session, as a committable scenario file and load it to put the app in a known state offline

Drive

  • Inject a push — most mobile journeys start with one, so LogPose delivers a synthetic FCM data message into the running app in-process (no Play services, no network). Re-send a captured push verbatim, or compose a new one
  • Trace waterfall — read a whole flow on one time axis: what the push set off, what overlapped, what is still running, and what took the longest
  • Correlation keys — group that flow by the id you actually know (order_id 21053953) rather than a trace hash. The key names a value; the value is matched anywhere in an event, so the group spans traces and reaches rows that carry none. Paste an id from a ticket with Find by value…

Requires the logpose-android interceptor in your debug/staging build (a zero-overhead no-op ships for release). Mocking needs logpose-android 1.2.1+; database, worker, config and app events need 1.4.0+; push injection and the new mock matchers/steps need 1.7.0+, and 1.7.1+ collapses an injected push and the app's own re-log of it into a single row. Correlation keys need no library support at all — they read the payloads you already emit. Works in IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio, light and dark.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Secrets stop leaking through query strings (library 1.7.3): sensitive query values (api_key, token, secret, …) are masked in the capture the way headers already were — the name stays, the value goes. Mock rules still match against the real values. FCM registration tokens truncate by default.
  • Device picker — with several devices attached, capture used to fail; a device: auto ▾ link in the toolbar now lists devices and remembers your choice per project. One device attached: nothing changes.
  • Search reads bodies — the list search now matches status codes and (for 3+ character queries) request/response bodies through the correlation cache, so typing never scans a payload.
  • Response-body privacy has a switch: the Connect Coding Agent panel can now withhold bodies from agents (payload_withheld over MCP).
  • Worker rows tell waiting apart from running (needs logpose-android 1.7.2). The fact column shows queued 6.2s and the time column is now the run duration rather than queue + run. The library remembers the enqueue and run-start instants itself, so upgrading the dependency is the whole integration — and when it never observed a queue phase (attached mid-flight, process restarted, row replayed from WorkManager) it shows nothing rather than guessing.
  • Each kind's row says the useful thing. A wall of repeated polling collapses to one line with an ×N pill, the median duration and an occurrence ‹ n/N › stepper in the detail (it breaks on any non-2xx — a failed poll always stands alone). DB rows lead with the verb and the table, with the full statement greyed behind them, and BEGIN/END ceremony folds into a single muted transaction ✓ · 4 statements · 128ms row. Worker rows state their state with shape and semantics — ✓ succeeded, ● running with a live count-up, ✕ failed, an outlined RETRY ×N — and surface the tag that tells one DataSyncWorker from another. Analytics rows drop the · ANALYTICS echo and put the screen in the fact column.
  • A systematic visual pass — one axis owns hue. Amber used to mean PUT, 4xx, db, warning, timeout and pending-sync at once. Now kind keeps the seven hues (row glyph, TYPE chip, detail pill, waterfall bars — nowhere else), status carries only semantics (2xx/3xx neutral, amber = warning, red = failure), method drops colour entirely and encodes read-vs-write by weight, and anything LogPose itself caused (MOCK, INJ) is the only solid accent fill in a row.
  • Rows reclaimed 46–92px each — FCM and structured rows no longer reserve empty method/status columns for a grid only HTTP uses. The hover ⧉ cURL and ⇉ flow affordances became real buttons that stay visible on the selected row instead of hiding until you hover.
  • The filter bar earns its space — search, type chips and the count stay; method, status, hide-noise and duplicates moved into a Filters popover with a badge, and every active choice echoes as a removable chip on a second row. That row is also where two previously silent behaviours finally explain themselves: "status filter → showing HTTP only" and "db hidden by default". Below ~440px the type chips collapse to glyphs.
  • "Filtered to nothing" is its own state — it names the count and the filter actually narrowing the list, and offers a loosener picked by measuring which one would reveal the most events, instead of showing the setup guide to someone who already has 218 events captured.
  • The waterfall got its first design pass — axis labels below the canvas, durations right-aligned in a fixed column, lanes sharing the list's selection model, and open spans pulsing on a smooth ease. (It also fixed a real bug: span bars were painting at 27% alpha instead of 70%.)
  • Group a flow by the id you actually know — define your app's correlation keys (order_id, trip_id) in the filter bar's ⋯ → Correlation keys…, seeded with suggestions found in the capture, and every entry point reads order_id 21053953 instead of a trace hash. The key only names a value; the value does the matching — anywhere in an event's url, bodies, FCM data, db args or sections — so a group spans several traces and reaches the GET /order/21053953/ that carries no trace at all. The scan parses JSON nested inside string values (an FCM data["body"]), and matching is delimiter-bounded with a 4-character floor, so 2105 never matches 21053953. Keys are per project; LogPose ships none of its own, and a suggestion groups nothing until you tick it.
  • Open a flow from anywhere — a row's menu leads with Show waterfall — order_id 21053953 and Filter by order_id 21053953 (trace actions still there, now labelled as traces); the hover band that shows ⧉ cURL also shows a ⇉ flow glyph that opens the row's best grouping in one click; the waterfall header states what it grouped by and offers a switcher between order_id / trip_id / trace; and a key filter appears as a removable chip. Find by value… needs no row at all: paste an id from a ticket or a backend log and it tells you how many events carry it before you commit.
  • Two new MCP tools (21 total) — get_related returns everything carrying one business id in get_trace's shape (by key + value, by a bare pasted value, or by event_id), and list_correlation_keys reports the configured vocabulary plus inert suggestions. get_trace now explains an empty result — an app that mints its own trace for a push, or an HTTP client not built with LogPose.traceCalls(...), is the usual reason — and points at get_related.
  • An injected push is one row again — the app's own FirebaseMessagingService re-logging a push LogPose injected used to add an unmarked twin beside it. With logpose-android ≥ 1.7.1 both emissions share the message id, so they collapse into one row that stays marked INJ. Note the consequence: the surviving row carries the app's trace rather than the injection's, which is one more reason to group these by key.
  • Start a flow, don't just watch it — right-click any captured push → Re-send this push, or Compose push… for a new one: LogPose delivers it into the running app in-process, no Play services and no network. Register LogPose.onPushInject { } in app init (or keep a FirebaseMessagingService in the manifest and LogPose finds it reflectively). Injected pushes appear as ordinary FCM rows marked INJ, and the device reports which tier consumed it. Simulates foreground data-message delivery — not the system notification tray. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.7.0.
  • Scenarios — save the current mocks, or snapshot the whole session, into a committable .logpose/scenarios/<name>.json, then load it to put the app in a known state offline. A snapshot builds one rule per endpoint from the latest real response, skips (and counts) endpoints with no completed response, and never re-serves LogPose's own mocked rows as if the backend had said them. Scenario files contain captured bodies — review before committing.
  • Trace waterfall — a new detail card lays a whole trace on one time axis: a lane per event, spans as bars, point events as dots, in-flight spans drawn out to now, with the event count, wall span and slowest event in the header. Open it from a row's context menu (Show waterfall) or by clicking the trace chip on any detail card; click a lane to jump to its row.
  • Richer mocks — an Only when… section matches on query parameters, headers and a request-body substring, and a Then respond… step list serves a different response per hit (500 then 200 tests retry logic in one rule). Body matching fails closed, so a body the device can't buffer goes to the network rather than being mocked on a guess. Rules using these are withheld from a device on an older library instead of being pushed and silently ignored. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.7.0.
  • Five new MCP tools (19 total) — await_event blocks until the event you're waiting for arrives, so an agent's loop becomes trigger → await → assert instead of polling list_events; inject_fcm sends or replays a push and returns the trace it delivered inside; list_scenarios / load_scenario / save_scenario expose the scenario files. create_mock gains match_query, match_headers, match_body_contains and responses.
  • The mocks strip tells the truth about sync — pushed revision vs the one the device acknowledged, so pending and failed read as pending and failed; a broadcast adb refused is caught (am prints errors and still exits 0); an ack that never arrives raises a notification instead of hijacking the detail pane; and the device's active rule count now surfaces the reinstall-reset case. "Loaded" is not "live", and the strip finally says which.
  • No-op parity is now enforced — the release stub had drifted (it was missing LogPoseInterceptor(config, emitter), so a custom sink compiled in debug and failed in release). Fixed, and a reflection parity test in the library build fails on the next drift.
  • Headless capture export for CI — with logpose-android ≥ 1.6.0 and LogPoseConfig(exportEnabled = true), scripts/export-capture.sh dumps the whole capture as NDJSON over adb, so a pipeline can assert on the wire with no IDE/MCP session. create_mock now warns when a timeout/ connection_failure has latency_ms = 0 (it throws instantly, testing the failure path, not an in-flight window), and a mocked request shows an in-flight row while its latency plays out. push-mocks.sh --verify reads the device ack back to confirm rules actually applied.
  • Async HTTP rows can join a trace — wrap a flow in LogPose.withTrace { } or traceContext() and, with the client set up via LogPose.traceCalls(...), the request's row lands in the same get_trace group as the flow's other events — even across a viewModelScope.launch. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.5.7.
  • Honest mock hit counts — list_mocks now reports served, counted from the captured mocked responses in the buffer, instead of the device counter that read 0 while a rule was demonstrably serving. create_mock's warning names the real precondition (restart the app so it announces itself to this capture). Ambient trace now also covers the FCM row itself, and LogPose.continueTrace { } carries a trace across a viewModelScope.launch — both need logpose-android ≥ 1.5.6.
  • Reliability & test-orchestration — capture now reports whether it's running (and auto-reattaches after an adb drop, so it no longer dies silently on a reinstall); create_mock warns loudly when no device is synced; a new clear_capture tool and a scripts/push-mocks.sh make the mocked tier runnable in CI; chatty analytics/DB feeds are capped so they can't evict the events you care about; and stale mocks are pruned on a new app run. Ambient trace scope LogPose.withTrace { } needs logpose-android ≥ 1.5.5.
  • Typed rows & detail — every row leads with a colour-coded type glyph (one hue per kind); non-network rows keep the method/status columns clear so the centre lines up, and the type is stated once instead of as a doubled, truncated pill. TYPE filter chips are lit in the matching hue, and the detail pane renders flat key/value data as a table.
  • Analytics on the timeline — LogPose.logAnalytics(...) puts every analytics event next to the API call and screen that fired it, with an ANLY filter chip. A new analytics_events MCP tool verifies event contracts and returns the observed screen-to-screen flow. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.5.4.
  • Quick mock diff — a diff button on each mock row opens the original captured response beside what the rule serves, without opening the editor first.
  • Replayed workers — WorkManager replays finished work from earlier runs to a fresh observer, which used to look like it ran again this session (why a worker could read as "20 runs on startup"). Those are now marked with a muted replayed badge, and worker_history splits "ran this session" from replays. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.5.3.
  • 1.7.1 — the coding-agent docs now lead with example prompts ("what failed in the last 2 minutes?", "mock /v1/orders to return a 500") so it's obvious what to ask. No behaviour change.
  • Sessions — a capture that spans an app restart is no longer reported as one timeline. Each run is reported separately, with its own span and counts, and list_events can be scoped to one run. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.5.0.
  • Wider redaction by default — credential headers beyond Authorization (API-KEY, X-Auth-Token, vendor tokens matched by name) are masked before anything leaves the device. Update logpose-android to pick this up.
  • Summaries you can act on — session_summary now returns the ids behind every failure and duplicate burst instead of bare counts, identical failures collapse into one entry with a count, and kinds that never fired report zero rather than going missing.
  • Database, background work and remote config on the timeline — the three things every Android app has, now first-class alongside HTTP and FCM. Room queries show their operation and table (users · SELECT id FROM users), a WorkManager request occupies one row that updates as it runs and badges its retries, and a remote-config activation reports exactly which flags changed, with before → after values. New DB / WORK / CONF filter chips, and MCP tools for "what's making this screen slow?", "did SyncWorker retry?" and "what flag changed before this broke?". Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.4.0.
  • Your coding agent can read the running app — LogPose now exposes the live capture over MCP, so Claude Code (or any MCP client) can answer "what did the app actually request, and why did it fail?" from real traffic instead of a pasted log line — and can create a mock to reproduce or unblock a state. Click ⚡ Connect Coding Agent to copy the command. Served on the IDE's built-in web server, localhost only, authenticated with a per-project token.
  • Log anything, not just HTTP — LogPose.event("UserDao.insert") { … } puts your own subsystems on the same timeline: database queries, background jobs, analytics, feature flags, navigation. Events carry their own presentation, so they render with no plugin update. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.4.0; older versions keep working unchanged.
  • New look — a redesigned brand mark (a prompt that points north), native IDE context menus, and a roomier, better-organised mock editor.
  • Field-by-field mock editing — edit a captured response as a tree: fold what you don't need, edit any value in place, and in merge mode tick exactly the fields to override (a changed value shows the original beside it). Add new keys, drop to raw text, or hit Compare with original for a side-by-side diff of what the app will actually receive.
  • Merge (patch) mocks — keep the real backend response and deep-merge your JSON on top: override one field, add keys, leave the rest untouched. Merging now recurses into arrays by index, so you can change a field inside data[0] without replacing the array. Needs logpose-android ≥ 1.2.1.
  • Mock & replay — right-click a captured request → "Mock this endpoint…" to serve a response back to the app instead of hitting the network: edit status/body/headers, add latency, or simulate a timeout / connection failure. Rules live in a Mocks strip (toggle, edit, delete, hit counts), persist per project, and mocked rows carry a purple MOCK pill. Requires logpose-android ≥ 1.1.0 on the device.
  • FCM push messages in the timeline — Firebase Cloud Messaging pushes and token refreshes now appear inline alongside HTTP traffic, tagged FCM with a NOTIF/DATA/TOKEN badge. Selecting one shows the notification, metadata, and the data payload as a JSON tree. A new TYPE filter (NET/FCM) narrows the stream. Feed events from your FirebaseMessagingService via the new LogPose.logFcmMessage / logFcmToken library API.
  • Failed requests now show why — instead of an opaque "(failed)", the Response and Overview cards display the captured exception (connection reset, timeout, cleartext-not-permitted, …) so the failure is diagnosable.
  • Duplicate-call detection — repeated identical requests fired in a quick burst are flagged with a DUP ×N tag; overlapping non-idempotent calls (double-submits) are highlighted in red, with a warning in the overview and a "Dupes" filter to isolate them.
  • Raw JSON now colors keys vs. values (matching the tree), shows line numbers, and pre-collapses deeply-nested nodes on large payloads.
  • Response headers are hidden by default behind a "Headers" toggle (request headers stay shown) — no more CSP noise drowning the body.
  • Light-theme support (adapts to the IDE theme)
  • Raw JSON mode is now a real editor with code folding
  • One-click filter bar (method/status toggles, Hide-noise switch)
  • Find in request/response, server trace-id in the overview
  • Multi-select rows and copy the call sequence as a plain-text timeline
  • Helpful empty state
